chunks: As for what Jābir ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī narrated, he said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a gecko falling into the well, and he said: It is nothing; stir the water with the bucket in the well.

So this does not contradict the first report, because the first report is to be understood as recommendation, and this report accords with what we have already presented from the reports: that whatever has no flowing blood does not spoil the water by its death, and the gecko is of that kind.

key_terms.السَّامُّ أَبْرَصُ: gecko; the creature discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: well; the water source in question
key_terms.حَرِّكِ الْمَاءَ: stir the water; the instructed action to take
key_terms.لَا يَفْسُدُ: it is not spoiled; meaning the water remains unaffected
key_terms.نَفْسٌ سَائِلَةٌ: flowing blood; a legal criterion affecting water impurity

ai.seo_question: Does a gecko falling into a well make the water impure?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a gecko falling into a well. It indicates that such an occurrence does not render the water spoiled, and the earlier report is reconciled as referring to recommendation rather than obligation.
